solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Beetles left in sand by holidaymakers

indicators.note: by means next to, so the holidaymakers stand beside the sand's letter
the leftmost letter in the word sand is wanted, its first

parts.note: people holidaying in tents or caravans are campers

explanation.surface: Footprints of little insects found on a beach after the tourists have gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beetles' looks like the insects but is a verb: to beetle along is to hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: To beetle is to scurry quickly, a verb synonym for running off in little rushes.

clue.text: Parrot with suitable protection

parts.note: to parrot is to repeat or imitate, to copy
suitable means right, as in the right person for the job

explanation.surface: A pet bird kept with the proper safeguards.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal protection for an author's work against reproduction is this form of intellectual property right.

clue.text: Army group butter up composer

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a unit is a group of soldiers
something that butts, a ram

explanation.surface: Soldiers flattering a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter up' looks like a phrase for flattery; 'butter' is the ram and 'up' signals the reversal. Bohuslav Martinů was a Czech composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bohuslav Martinů was a twentieth-century Czech writer of symphonies and operas.

clue.text: Finish burlesque topless

indicators.note: without its top, so in a down clue the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a burlesque is a parody, a send-up

explanation.surface: The close of a striptease show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' fits the burlesque stage, but here it just removes the first letter S.
explanation.definitionFit: To finish somewhere is to land there eventually, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Father's abbreviated title

indicators.note: shortened by losing its final letter

parts.note: Father's is read as father is; a father is a sire

explanation.surface: Dad's honour written in short form.
explanation.definitionFit: A form of address used for a knight or baronet, a courtesy rank before a name.

clue.text: Islander, famous at last, with a grouse

indicators.note: only the last letter of famous is used

parts.note: to grouse is to complain, to moan

explanation.surface: A Pacific islander who finally became famous and has a complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Polynesian islands of the South Pacific is an example of an islander.

clue.text: Half-hearted beggar wandering amid fat farmer's crop

indicators.note: amid means the shuffled letters are placed in the middle of the fat

parts.note: suet is hard animal fat

indicators.note: wandering about, so the letters move into a new order
one of the two middle letters, the heart, is removed

explanation.surface: A feeble tramp roams through a farmer's field of produce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-hearted' drops one G from BEGGAR, leaving BEGAR; 'wandering' turns that into GARBE, which goes 'amid' SUET.
explanation.definitionFit: A root vegetable grown on farms as a source of sucrose is this kind of crop.

clue.text: Unsteady creature holding another up

indicators.note: the first creature holds the second inside it

parts.note: a mule is a hybrid animal

indicators.note: in a down clue the second creature is written bottom to top

parts.note: another creature, here a bat

explanation.surface: A wobbly animal carrying a second one on its back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses BAT to TAB, which MULE holds.
explanation.definitionFit: Something changeable and liable to alter is unsteady in the sense of not fixed.

clue.text: See eye to eye about occupying time

indicators.note: the word for about occupies, sits inside, the word for time

parts.note: an age is a long period of time
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Two people find common ground on how to fill their time.
explanation.definitionFit: To see eye to eye is an idiom for holding the same opinion as someone.

clue.text: Pole not used has end missing

indicators.note: the final letter is taken off

parts.note: something not used is spare

explanation.surface: An unused stick that's lost its tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' could suggest a Polish person; it is a stout pole such as a mast.
explanation.definitionFit: A stout rod used as a mast or boom on a ship is a nautical pole.

clue.text: Insulting aged or corrupt politician

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled or altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Abuse aimed at an elderly or dishonest politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupt' rearranges AGED OR into DEROGA.
explanation.definitionFit: Remarks that belittle or disparage someone are offensive, a synonym of insulting.

clue.text: A ruling on British intelligence

indicators.note: in an across clue on means placed after, so these pieces follow the British letters

parts.note: a ruling party is in power

explanation.surface: A court decision about British spying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A ruling' looks like a court decision; it is A plus IN POWER.
explanation.definitionFit: Mental capacity or cleverness is the sense of intelligence meant here.

clue.text: Western composer, not the first recorded

indicators.note: the composer's name loses its first letter

parts.note: Benjamin Britten was an English composer

explanation.surface: A cowboy-film composer who didn't come top in the charts.
explanation.definitionFit: Something set down on paper or in a record is put in writing.

clue.text: Raised part of garden Rex installed

indicators.note: installed means put in place inside the garden part

parts.note: a flower bed is part of a garden
R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A raised garden bed built by the king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' seems to describe the bed but is the definition, as in brought up.
explanation.definitionFit: Children who are raised are brought up, a past-participle synonym.

clue.text: About 500 guineas collected for a piece of music

indicators.note: about means turned around, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: Roughly five hundred guineas raised for a musical work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'approximately' but rearranges D and GUINEAS; 'collected for' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin prayer 'Lamb of God' is set to music as part of the Mass.

clue.text: Breaking of law avoids plea of not guilty?

indicators.note: breaking up the words, so their letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A defendant who broke the law dodges entering a not-guilty plea.
explanation.definitionFit: Denying responsibility for an act is a repudiation, which the question mark flags as a loose plea.

clue.text: Spared parliamentarian in city abandoned by monarch

indicators.note: the parliamentarian goes inside the shortened city
the monarch's letters leave the city name

parts.note: Exeter is a cathedral city in Devon
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An MP in a city left by the Queen got off lightly.
explanation.walkthrough: EXETER less ER leaves EXET; MP goes 'in' it. Exeter is a city in Devon, south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone excused from a duty or obligation has been let off it.

clue.text: Choosing to tour East Riding — primarily to see a part of Yorkshire

indicators.note: the choosing word goes round the next letters

parts.note: choosing is picking

indicators.note: only the first letter of Riding is used

explanation.surface: Choosing a sightseeing trip around Yorkshire's East Riding.
explanation.walkthrough: Pickering is a market town in North Yorkshire; the East Riding is a historic division of Yorkshire. 'to see' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A market town on the edge of the North York Moors, so a part of that county.

clue.text: Fiction ignoring current provisions

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out the letter for current

parts.note: fiction consists of stories
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Novels that disregard what's going on now.
explanation.definitionFit: Supplies of food kept for future use are provisions, a plural synonym.

clue.text: Bird list has to include duck

indicators.note: the list must take the duck inside it

parts.note: a roster is a list of duties
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

explanation.surface: A register of birds must feature a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' looks like another bird but is O, a nil score in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A male domestic fowl, a cockerel, is a farmyard bird.

clue.text: Tailcoat regularly worn by the same lake

indicators.note: worn by means inside, the way clothing is inside its wearer

parts.note: the same letters again, those taken from Tailcoat

indicators.note: every other letter of Tailcoat, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A tailcoat worn by the same person beside a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks TICA from Tailcoat; a second copy of TICA wears it.
explanation.definitionFit: The large lake in the Andes on the border of Peru and Bolivia.

clue.text: Material to line empty cupboards or drawers?

indicators.note: the material lines, goes inside, the emptied word
an empty word keeps only its outer letters

parts.note: rayon is a synthetic fabric

explanation.surface: Fabric for lining bare cupboards or chests of drawers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawers' looks like furniture but means things that draw, with the question mark flagging the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Coloured wax sticks are things one draws with, so whimsically they are drawers.

clue.text: What about constant love for parrot?

indicators.note: the word for What goes about, around, the constant

parts.note: eh? means what?
c is the constant for the speed of light
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about steady affection for a pet bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parrot' is a verb here, to repeat.
explanation.definitionFit: To repeat what was said, as a sound reflected back does, is to parrot it.

clue.text: Officer's demeanour in capital

indicators.note: the demeanour goes in, inside, the officer

parts.note: CO is a commanding officer
an air is a manner or demeanour

explanation.surface: An officer's bearing in a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of Egypt, on the Nile.

clue.text: Rude sign shown to be justified

parts.note: the V-sign is a rude gesture in Britain
shown means indicated

explanation.surface: A rude gesture proved to be warranted.
explanation.walkthrough: The V-sign, two fingers raised with the palm inward, is an insult in Britain. 'to be' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone cleared of blame or proved right has been shown correct.

clue.text: Some aeroplanes Biggles sent up for playfellow

indicators.note: in a down clue sent up means read from bottom to top
some of the letters of these words, a run inside them

explanation.surface: Biggles launches a few planes for a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: Biggles is a fictional British flying ace from boys' stories. 'playfellow' is a fellow who writes plays.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen, the Norwegian dramatist, is jokingly a fellow of plays.

clue.text: Cat, short one, comes to birds

indicators.note: short means the last letter is lopped off

parts.note: kitty is a pet name for a cat
I is the Roman numeral one
to come to is to regain consciousness, to wake

explanation.surface: A cat and a small creature approach some birds.
explanation.definitionFit: These are seabirds of the gull family, named for their call.

clue.text: Non-European cattle may be related

indicators.note: the letter for European is removed

parts.note: kine is an old plural of cow

explanation.surface: Cattle from outside Europe might be of one family.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, the word means of the same family, connected by blood.

clue.text: State different bits after zero hour

indicators.note: the bits come after the zero hour letters

parts.note: zero looks like the letter O
the two different binary bits, 1 and 0, look like I and O

explanation.surface: Assorted pieces after midnight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different bits' looks like an anagram signal; it means the two binary digits.
explanation.definitionFit: A midwestern US state on Lake Erie.

clue.text: Penitent pruned the Spanish chestnut

indicators.note: cut back, so the end letter is trimmed

parts.note: penitent means sorry
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A sorry gardener cut back the Spanish chestnut tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chestnut' suggests the tree but is a horse colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A reddish-brown horse colour, which chestnut also names.

clue.text: Failure to utilise common herb

parts.note: non-U means not upper class, so common
sage is a herb

explanation.surface: Not using an everyday herb.
explanation.walkthrough: Non-U is British slang for not upper-class, from a 1950s essay on class speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Not employing something is a lack of use, the noun for failing to use.
